{{1980 Pacific-10 Conference football standings}}
The '''1980 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University]] as a member of the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pacific-10 Conference]] (Pac-10) during the [[1980 NCAA Division I-A football season]] In their first season under head coach [[Joe Avezzano]], the Beavers compiled an overall record of 0–11 with a mark of 0–8 in conference play, finished last in the Pac-10, and were outscored by their opponents 386 to 108.<ref>{{cite web|title=1980 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=SR/College Football|access-date=September 7, 2016|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/1980-schedule.html}}</ref> The team played four home games on campus at [[Reser Stadium|Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon]].

Avezzano, previously the offensive coordinator at [[1979 Tennessee Volunteers football team|Tennessee]] under [[Johnny Majors]], was hired in late 1979;<ref name=bsvav>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=tgYzAAAAIBAJ&sjid=EuIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6454%2C50933 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |title=Beavers select Vols' Avezanno |date=December 1, 1979 |page=1B}}</ref> he succeeded [[Craig Fertig]] and signed a four-year contract at $40,000 per year.<ref name=tpfos>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=jtIvAAAAIBAJ&sjid=LPkDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2331%2C79203 |work=Spokane Daily Chronicle |location=Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=Tennessee aide pick for Oregon State job |date=December 1, 1979 |page=13}}</ref><!-- "[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=lYouAAAAIBAJ&sjid=cYcFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4553,257144 Tri-City Herald]"  ''– Oregon State selects new head football coach'' Associated Press – December 2, 1979 – p.54-->
